data.name: Satvik
data.gender_notes: Satvik is used as a masculine name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Satvik comes from the Sanskrit word 'Satva', which means truth or goodness. It is one of the three gunas, or fundamental qualities of the universe, and represents purity, truth, and knowledge. A satvik person is one who is pure, truthful, and possesses wisdom and knowledge. The name Satvik carries the meaning “Truthful, Pure, Good” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Hindi. Parents who choose Satvik usually hope their child will grow to embody truthful, pure, good and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.cultural_impact: The term Satvik holds significant importance in Hinduism, as it represents the ideal state of being. In Hindu philosophy, the world is seen as a manifestation of three fundamental qualities or gunas: Satva, Rajas, and Tamas. Satvik, derived from Satva, symbolizes purity, wisdom, and peace. It is often used to describe food, lifestyle, and behaviors that align with these qualities. For instance, satvik food is described as being pure, fresh, and organic, promoting good health and a clear mind.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, being satvik is considered to be a desirable state of being as it represents purity, truth, and knowledge - all qualities that are essential for spiritual growth and enlightenment. A satvik person is one who strives for truth and knowledge, promotes peace and harmony, and radiates positive energy. They are often seen as being closer to the divine, as their actions and thoughts align with the universal principle of truth and goodness. In essence, Satvik serves as a reminder of the importance of living a truthful and pure life, and striving for wisdom and knowledge to deepen our spiritual connection with the universe.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Satvik denotes one who embodies truth, purity, and righteousness in thoughts, words, and actions. It represents the path of wisdom, harmony, and self-realization in Hindu philosophy.
